Author: Klubthawee N, Adisakwattana P, Hanpithakpong W, Somsri S, Aunpad R
Comments: Function: PA-13 exhibited potent antibacterial activity against P. aeruginosa, including multidrug resistant strains, via penetration through the bacteria’s membrane and causing depolarization, permeabilization and rupture of membranes, and subsequent leakage of intracellular contents and cell death. The peptide displayed low hemolytic and cytotoxic activities against mammalian cells suggesting a therapeutic potential. Furthermore, PA-13 showed anti-inflammatory activity via LPS neutralization. Note: It maintained antimicrobial activity in the presence of physiological salts and displayed rapid binding and penetration activity which resulted in membrane depolarization and permeabilization.?
Cytotoxicity: [Ref.32499514]Cytotoxic activity of PA-13 against the L929 mouse fibroblast cell line was determined by a colorimetric MTT viability assay. At the MIC (3.91??g/ml), the cell survival was up to 90%. Even at the maximum concentration (250??g/ml), the survival was common (81.29%). Melittin, used as a positive control, showed a strong and dose-dependent cytotoxic effect; no living cells were detected at 62.5??g/ml. Peptide PA-13 displayed very little cytotoxicity on L929 cells when compared to melittin.
Hemolytic_activity: [Ref.32499514]MHC = 125 μg/mL. Note:MHC is the minimum concentration that caused 10% hemolysis of human red blood cells (hRBC). When no 10% hemolysis was observed at 250??g/ml, a value of 500??g/ml was used to calculate the therapeutic index.
Name: PA-13
Target_Organism: [Ref.32499514] Gram-negative bacteria: Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC = 3.91 ?g/ml), Escherichia coli ATCC 25922 (MIC = 31.25 ?g/ml), Escherichia coli O157:H7 MT strain (MIC = 31.25 ?g/ml), Shigella sonnei ATCC 11060 (MIC = 3.91 ?g/ml), Salmonella Typhimurium ATCC 13311 (MIC = 1.95 ?g/ml), Vibrio cholera O1 Inaba DMST 16261 (MIC = 31.25 ?g/ml), Acinetobacter baumannii MT strain (MIC = 7.81 ?g/ml). ##Clinically isolated MDR P. aeruginosa: P. aeruginosa No.1 (3.91 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.2 (7.81μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.3 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.4 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.5 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.6 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.7 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.8 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.9 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.10 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.11 (7.81 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.12 (3.91 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.13 (15.63 μg/mL), P. aeruginosa No.14 (7.81 μg/mL),##Gram-positive bacteria:Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC = 62.5 ?g/ml) Staphylococcus epidermidis ATCC 12228 (MIC = 3.91 ?g/ml), Bacillus cereus ATCC 11778 (MIC = 15.63 ?g/ml), Enterococcus faecalis ATCC 29212 (MIC = 250 ?g/ml), Listeria monocytogenes 10403?s (MIC = 3.91 ?g/ml)
